sources.excerpt: Dundee cake is a traditional Scottish fruit cake.
Simnel cake is a fruitcake associated with Lent and Easter and widely eaten in the United Kingdom, Ireland and countries with patterns of migration from them.
Battenberg or Battenburg cake is a light sponge cake with coloured sections held together with jam and covered in marzipan.
The Bakewell tart is a traditional English cake originating in the town of Bakewell, in the Derbyshire Dales district of Derbyshire.
The city of Stirling has the smallest population amongst Scotland's cities, with an estimated population of just over 37,000 inhabitants.
Today, Perth serves as a retail centre for the surrounding area, and in 2018 the city was named "Scotland's Food Town of 2018" by the Scottish Food Awards.
Inverness is a city in the Scottish Highlands in the north of Scotland.
Aberdeen is a port city in North East Scotland, and is the third most populous Scottish city.

The River Tay ( ; Scottish Gaelic: Tatha, IPA: [ˈt̪ʰa.ə]; probably from the conjectured Brythonic Tausa, possibly meaning 'silent one' or 'strong one' or, simply, 'flowing') is the longest river in Scotland and the seventh-longest in Great Britain.
Its catchment is approximately 2,000 square miles (5,200 square kilometres), the Tweed's is 1,500 sq mi (3,900 km2) and the Spey's is 1,097 sq mi (2,840 km2).
The river rises in the Lowther Hills and flows north-west through South Lanarkshire and Glasgow before deepening into the Firth of Clyde past the Tail of the Bank off Greenock.
The River Forth is a major river in central Scotland, 47 km (29 mi) long, which drains into the North Sea on the east coast of the country.
